exemplars.title: Prompting Destiny: Negotiating Socialization and Growth in an LLM-Mediated Speculative Gameworld
exemplars.why: The system explicitly suppresses real-time evaluation during play and releases feedback only at the end-of-stage boundary, with a stated rationale—reducing score-chasing—for choosing deferral over continuous intervention.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Unlike TeamVision, this paper explicitly establishes both deliberate withholding during the activity and release at a defined boundary, rather than merely locating a dashboard after the activity.

exemplars.title: TeamVision: An AI-powered Learning Analytics System for Supporting Reflection in Team-based Healthcare Simulation
exemplars.why: Its post-simulation analytics dashboard plausibly creates the pattern’s two phases: an uninterrupted simulation followed immediately by a dedicated debrief using information derived from that simulation. The supplied evidence, however, does not explicitly confirm silent observation or retroactive controls.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Unlike PRISM, TeamVision presents an analytics surface tied to the completed activity, offering stronger evidence that findings were derived from phase one and exposed in a distinct phase two.

exemplars.title: PRISM: Post-task Reflection via Intelligent Social Multi-agents for Enhancing Learning Experience and Industrial Skill Retention
exemplars.why: PRISM clearly reserves its assistance for a post-task phase and restructures the completed experience into reflective dialogue, but the evidence does not establish during-task detection, intentional withholding, or controls that revise phase-one material.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Unlike the meeting-feedback candidate, PRISM transforms material from the completed task into a defined post-task intervention rather than beginning a new solicitation process only after the activity.

notes: The consensus ordering is retained, but all three scores are reduced because none fully demonstrates the complete structural signature, especially findings paired with controls that retroactively revise phase-one material. PRISM receives the largest adjustment, from 2.40 to 2.10, because one rater’s structural disqualification is persuasive: post-task reflection alone is not deferred intervention. Readers should distrust any inference beyond the quoted evidence: 9513 is supported only by an abstract excerpt, TeamVision only by a brief abstract statement, and PRISM only by a figure caption. TeamVision’s silent accumulation is inferred rather than shown, while PRISM’s during-task detection is not evidenced at all. The fourth candidate was excluded because it solicits feedback after the meeting rather than revealing an intervention generated and withheld during it.
